liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **New Speedway Boogie** (5 reviews, 1 other source): Described as the earliest known version, with harmonies badly off-key yet seemingly intentional and sarcastic; Identified as the first known performance of the song [1][2][5][7][8][10]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): China Cat into Rider has high energy for the period; The China Cat/Rider jams are praised as fiery [5][10]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (2 reviews): Above average, with an unusual rap containing some shocking elements; Pigpen delivers a classic rant of relationship advice, and the tape cuts out in the middle of it [5][9]
- **High Time** (1 review): Reviewer finds this performance rough and a bit hard to listen to [2]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): The jam in The Eleven is praised as fiery [10]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: New Speedway Boogie [14]

## The recordings

- **gd69-12-20.sbd.cotsman.6301.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 7 songs; 66 min; rated 2.55/5 by 20 [1]. Said about its sound: Good overall, with tape hiss between songs and what sounds like CD skipping during China Cat; Sound quality is poor, with skipping and popping, which the reviewer excuses given the tape's age [2][6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer notes this show and the 29th Fillmore show both claim to be the first acoustic show because Bill was late [3]
- Reviewer considers this not the best of the band's 1969 Fillmore performances [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-12-20.sbd.cotsman.6301.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Paul Hartman and JCotsman; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: This copy is incomplete: several songs between High Time and The Eleven are missing, possibly from vault reels too; Dark Star and Saint Stephen are cut from this recording; Missing reels were later found, and the complete show was released as Dave's Picks Volume 6 [1][8][12]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Fillmore, Dec. '69 Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1969/artwork/fillmore-dec-69-poster) [15]
